visual_brief.subject: Microsoft MXC gives local coding agents a policy boundary across operating systems
verified_context: Microsoft made MXC generally available as a policy-driven containment layer for untrusted workloads.
A workload can be granted access to selected files and network destinations without controlling the policy that defines its own authority.
GitHub now uses MXC-backed local sandboxing for Copilot tools across Windows, macOS, and Linux.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: The trusted policy boundary stays physically outside the active workload and constrains every path the workload can take.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A compact working chamber inside three nested architectural shells, with only a few deliberately shaped channels passing through aligned gates that are controlled from outside.
must_show: a small number of externally controlled access channels
clear physical separation between workload and policy boundary

candidate_notes.A: Selected. Three nested physical shells surround one active chamber while a small number of channels pass through exterior gates. The metaphor directly expresses externally controlled authority, remains legible at thumbnail size, and strongly matches the production archive's palette and architectural materiality.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant. The exterior mechanisms and protected chamber communicate enforcement, but the rocky vault and cable fittings are busier and more industrial than the quieter golden-reference set.
candidate_notes.C: Constitution-compliant. The nested material layers and external locking mass are clear, but the key-like silhouette narrows the meaning toward a single lock rather than a reusable policy boundary.

crop_review.article_desktop: 1100 x 591 center-cover review preserves all three shells, the inner chamber, and the exterior gates.
crop_review.article_mobile: 359 x 193 center-cover review retains the nested boundary and active center as the dominant idea.
crop_review.thumbnail: 320 x 164 review preserves the concentric silhouette and terracotta access channels without relying on fine detail.

golden_reference_comparison: Direct review beside the OpenAI DNS sandbox and Claude Code permission-hardening production assets shows the same warm paper ground, charcoal structural masses, sparing terracotta emphasis, physical security metaphor, controlled perspective, and crop-resilient central silhouette. Candidate A is denser and more symmetrical than the especially airy DNS reference, so golden-reference fit is scored at 88 rather than near-identical.
